- Plan §3 Kill criterion + §4.5 read 1 + §6.5 name `#667 gate_chain.clustered_bootstrap_spearman` as the family-clustered 95% CI for the headline DV `Δ_{r_B}/floor_SD`. The helper at `src/explore_persona_space/analysis/issue667/gate_chain.py:433` computes `spearman_rho(x, y)` between two paired arrays under family resampling — NOT a CI on a scalar location statistic.
- The headline DV is a per-cell scalar Δ/floor; there is no (x, y) array pair to correlate. Routing it through this helper either errors on the shape assert (line 451) or computes the wrong quantity. The §3 Kill criterion is un-executable as written.
- **Fix:** add a new `scripts/issue722_bootstrap.py` (or extend gate_chain) with a `clustered_bootstrap_scalar(values, families, statistic, n_boot, ...)` that resamples the 7 `target_cid` families with replacement and returns percentile / basic CI on the chosen scalar statistic of the per-context Δ values (state explicitly: mean or median). RESERVE `clustered_bootstrap_spearman` for the chain-ρ co-primary read ONLY. Update §3 Kill criterion + §4.5 read 1 + §6.5 to cite the new helper.
- Also name the scalar summary (mean vs median) the headline CI is taken over — the plan currently does not.

### MF#2 — M⁺ extrapolation off its own support is not nulled out (Methodology Codex; Claude raised it as Concern #1 but mis-classed as analyzer-weighable; reconciler upheld REVISE)
- M0 is fit on `(c0 → v0)` and evaluated at `c0` (in-support).
- M⁺ is fit on `(cplus = c_C_postft → vplus)` and evaluated at the SAME `c0` grid → off-support by exactly the c0↔cplus shift.
- The refit floor (§3/§11) is `‖M0_refit_a(c0) − M0_refit_b(c0)‖` — two in-support refits of M0 — and contains NO M⁺-off-support extrapolation term. At n≈16 against a 64-dim output, a high-dim ridge/MLP evaluated off-support can read above-floor even when the true function is unchanged → false H_function under H_input.
- **Fix:** add a **same-function shifted-design null** (call it `floor_shifted`): fit a pseudo-post map `M_pseudo: cplus → M0(cplus)` (i.e. shift the input to `cplus` but keep the SAME M0 function) through the identical bootstrap/refit harness, compute `‖M_pseudo(c0) − M0(c0)‖`, and take its 95th percentile as `floor_shifted`. Gate H_function on Δ exceeding BOTH the refit floor AND `floor_shifted`. Also report support-distance diagnostics (`‖cplus − c0‖` per cell) alongside Δ, and treat large-shift cells with extra caution (or exclude from H_function if `‖cplus − c0‖` exceeds a pre-registered threshold). Carry this into the §3 Kill criterion + the §6 hero figure.

### MF#3 — `eval` intent ≠ H100 under GCP-first routing (Methodology Codex)
- Plan §0/§9/§10 name "1× H100 (`eval` intent)" and cost the MLP ensemble on H100 ("<1 h on H100").
- Ground truth: `src/explore_persona_space/backends/gcp.py` `INTENT_TO_MACHINE["eval"]` = `g2-standard-4` (1× L4), NOT H100. Standing default is GCP-first.
- The 6 GPU-h MLP estimate is costed on H100, not the routed L4. The plan will silently dispatch to L4 (slower, possibly OOM on the MLP-batched LOCO ensemble) or fail under GCP routing.
- **Fix:** pin a real H100-capable intent explicitly. The repo exposes `eval-h100` and `lora-7b-h100` (gcp.py:314-323, SPOT/FLEX_START). Use one of those (`eval-h100` is the closest match) AND state the lane explicitly in §9 + §10. Alternatively, recost the entire MLP fit on L4 with chunk size + wall time + the `--max-run-duration` fence reconciled. Pin a CONCRETE single GPU-h number for the chosen lane.

### MF#4 — M0-only refit floor → also refit M⁺, gate on combined floor (Alternatives Codex)
- Same surface as MF#2 but a different statistical concern: even ignoring covariate shift, the noise floor `‖M0_refit_a − M0_refit_b‖` only captures M0's refit variance. The headline Δ = `‖M⁺(c) − M0(c)‖` propagates BOTH M0's and M⁺'s refit variance. If σ_M⁺ > σ_M0 (very plausible at n=16 on a post-FT-reshaped input geometry per the plan's own LOW-confidence §12), the M0-only floor is too tight → false H_function under true null.
- **Fix:** also refit M⁺ on bootstrap-over-cells + random-init through the identical harness, compute `floor_Mplus = 95th pct of ‖M⁺_refit_a(c0) − M⁺_refit_b(c0)‖`, report BOTH `floor_M0` and `floor_Mplus` in the artifact + the §6 hero figure caption, and gate H_function on Δ exceeding `max(floor_M0, floor_Mplus, floor_shifted)` (combining MF#2 and MF#4 fixes). Update §3 Kill criterion accordingly.

### Rationale
Codex was substantially right; Claude's CONCERNS undersells four registered-read defects that the analyzer pipeline cannot recover from. Verified against the plan + code:

- **MF#4, MF#5, MF#6, Claude Major#2 are Real & blocking** — each corrupts the pre-registered H-call / co-primary inference:
  - **MF#6** (`bootstrap.py:92-135`): `make_refit_pair` takes no `families` arg and does `idx = rng.integers(0, n, size=n)` — i.i.d. ROW bootstrap. Plan §4.5.1 line 122 registers the floors as "bootstrap-over-cells (resample contexts with replacement, **family-clustered**)". The headline Δ CI (`clustered_bootstrap_scalar`) IS family-clustered, so the H_function gate compares a family-clustered numerator against a row-bootstrapped floor — mismatched sampling units at n≈16 / 7 families understate the floor's family-level variance and bias the gate.
  - **MF#5** (`analyze.py:64-75`): `_h_call` reads only `Delta_med_ci` + `floor_combined`. The `Delta_med_excl_large_shift_ci` (computed at `fit_M.py:269`, threaded into the deliverable) is never consulted, so the H call can still report H_function even when the plan §3 / §4.5 support-distance robustness exclusion would flip it to H_mixed/inconclusive.
  - **MF#4** (`fit_M.py:288`): `rho_diff_ridge` point estimate is computed but no paired CI; output carries only `ci_M0_ridge` + `ci_Mplus_ridge`. Plan §6.5 line 215 + the §3 concordance check need the paired ρ-shift CI to call H_function with confidence; two marginal CIs do not test the paired difference.
  - **Claude Major#2** (`analyze.py:159-165`): `straddle_count` counts `H_input` toward the kill, so a clean 3×H_input result — the pre-registered positive outcome (plan line 74) explicitly NOT a failure per §3 line 234 ("an all-inside-floor result across all 3 behaviors with a passing shuffle check IS the H_input answer") — flags `inconclusive=True`. The per-cell `h_call` stays correct; the aggregate verdict is wrong.
- **MF#3** (`analyze.py:183`): writes `chain_rho.json` where plan §6.5 line 214 globs `chain_rho_M0_Mplus.json`; the deliverable-collection/promotion glob misses the co-primary file. Mechanical but breaks the registered deliverable contract.
- **MF#1** is REAL but NOT headline-blocking: plan §4.5 read 1 line 121 names the MLP Δ(c) for "both ridge and MLP," but plan §3 line 79 registers the ridge-only path as the PRIMARY headline (MLP-validity kill → ridge-only fallback "primary, not contingency"), and the H_function call (lines 14/68) gates purely on the ridge Δ_med vs floor_combined. The MLP still feeds the chain-ρ + nonlinearity-gap reads (which the code DOES compute). So the omitted MLP fixed-input Δ is a scope-narrowing to disclose as a clean-result caveat, not a headline-corrupting omission. It carries forward as a Must-Fix to either restore the MLP Δ read or document the deviation, but it is not the load-bearing FAIL.
- **MF#2 is a misread and is discarded.** Plan §4.5.1 line 124 registers `floor_shifted = median_c |(M_pseudo_a(c0) − M_pseudo_b(c0))·r̂_B|` — two equally-weak pseudo-refits at the base grid, so refit noise cancels (line 125), consistent with the other two floors. That is EXACTLY what `fit_M.py:247` + `bootstrap.py:130` compute. Codex's "intended" `M_pseudo(c0) − M0(c0)` is the §3 narrative of what the floor *captures off-support* (line 66), NOT the registered construction. No defect.
- **Claude Major#1 (CPU device)** is real: `_ridge_fit_predict`/`_mlp_loco_pred` read `fit658.DEVICE` (default `"cpu"`, `issue658:141`), flipped only inside `fit658.main()` via `_resolve_device`, which #722's `main()` never calls — so ridge AND the MLP ensemble run on CPU even on the 2×H100 `eval-h100` lane. Correctness is unaffected (plan asserts device-invariant DV) but it blows the ~11 GPU-h budget and idles the GPU; carries forward as a Must-Fix.

Net: ≥4 real blocking defects (MF#4/5/6 + Claude#2) on the registered H-call / co-primary inference + 2 mechanical/perf Must-Fixes (MF#3, Claude#1) → FAIL. This is round 1 of 3; bounce to implementer round 2 with the union Must-Fix list below.

## Interpretation Critique — Round 1

**Verdict: REVISE**

The fact result is genuinely clean and well-supported (Δ/floor_combined=3.3×, chain-ρ −0.12→+0.50 with M⁺ CI [+0.31,+0.64] and Δρ CI [+0.47,+0.72] both excluding zero at L14, holding at L21). But the body's TITLE, its CONFIDENCE TAG, and its HERO FIGURE all overclaim past what the kill criterion (`inconclusive`) and the two-denominator data support. Five must-fix items below.

### Overclaims

- **Title asserts a clean H_input for EM that the data does NOT certify.** H1 + frontmatter (lines 2-3, 28): "...while finetuning EM only moves the input the function reads." But `function_change.json.kill_criterion.per_behavior.em = "H_input_shuffle_failed"` and `outcome = "inconclusive"` — EM is NOT certified as H_input; the body's own Result-5 (line 149) and Takeaway #6 say so. The title states the inconclusive arm as a positive finding. — mechanizable: partial (a verifier could flag a title clause naming a behavior the kill_criterion marks `*_shuffle_failed`).
- **Takeaway #1 headline "9.5× the noise floor" is the wrong denominator.** Line 33/100: fact L14 is **3.3× the floor** (Δ=0.3125 / floor_combined=0.0949) and **9.5× the floor's SD** (`Delta_over_floor_sd`). The h_call / kill-criterion uses Δ/floor_combined; the heatmap plots Δ/floor_SD. Narrating "9.5× the noise floor" reports the SD-denominator number as if it were the floor itself — the metric narrated as the construct. State both denominators; lead with 3.3× (the one the verdict is built on).
- **"clearing it at all three layers" (Takeaway #1) overstates fact/L21.** fact/L21 Δ/floor_combined = **1.58** (barely above the floor); its H_function call rides on the looser floor_SD test (4.6×). Soften to "clears the combined floor cleanly at L7 and L14 (2.9–3.3×) and marginally at L21 (1.6×)."
- **"EM near-floor reading" (line 102) minimizes a below-floor result.** EM L14 Δ/floor_combined = 0.64 is BELOW the floor, not "near" it. Call it what it is.

### Surprising Unmentioned Patterns

- **The hero (Δ/floor_SD) and the raw companion (Δ vs floor_combined) tell OPPOSITE stories for EM and syco-L14, and the body never reconciles them.** In `function_change_delta_vs_floor.png` the EM-L14 and EM-L21 blue (Δ) bars sit visibly BELOW their orange (floor) bars, and syco-L14 Δ≈floor — yet the hero shows EM 2.1×/2.4× and syco-L14 3.5× (all "above 1×"). A reader who trusts the hero concludes EM cleared the floor; the raw plot (and the h_call) says it did not.
- **Every v0-reconstruction ρ is near-zero or NEGATIVE** (`nonlinearity_gap` + `chain_rho` `rho_M0_mlp`/`rho_M0_shuffle`). The "fact L7 beats shuffle by 0.002" claim (line 148) is a win of −0.078 over −0.080 — both are noise. Worth one sentence that even the "winning" cell isn't reconstructing.
- **cross_transfer: both M0→v⁺ and M⁺→v⁺ cosines are near-zero negative (−0.01 to −0.11).** The "added orthogonal structure" read rests entirely on M⁺→v0 being more negative (−0.22 to −0.32) than M⁺→v⁺ (≈0). When both reference predictions are ~0, "orthogonal" is hard to distinguish from "both maps are just weak."

### Alternative Explanations Not Addressed

- **The fact chain-ρ +0.50 may be inflated by effective-n ≪ 480.** The substrate concern (`substrate-context-vec-keyed-to-source`): the 30 targets per source share one `c_C`, so the chain-ρ correlates ~16 distinct inputs against E, not 480. The family-clustered CI over 7 families mitigates but does not fully price this. The body must surface this where the +0.50 CI is stated (Takeaway #4 + Result 3), not bury it in the methodology table (line 62).
- **Per-cell Δ_med bootstrap CIs are degenerate (point=lo=hi) in EVERY cell** (`function_change.json`, e.g. em/L14 ci_lo==ci_hi==point). The body's captions invoke "family-clustered bootstrap over 7 context families" (line 111) without disclosing that the per-cell CI collapsed to a point — the cross-behavior synthesis carries the inference, not any per-cell interval. State this honestly.
- **The "orthogonal, not rotation" claim** does not rule out that M⁺ is simply a noisier fit of the same target (weak maps everywhere); address the weak-map alternative explicitly.

### Confidence Calibration
